artifacts.notes: Normalized transcription, not a facsimile or critical edition. Historical Latin wording is public domain in the United States; portal markup and translations have separate rights. Historical witness: Acta Apostolicae Sedis 21 (1929), pp. 553-554. Uncollated normalized web transcription; source wording and numbering retained apart from the explicitly recorded corrections and apparatus exclusions. The source index and filename suggest 20 February 1929, but both the Latin body and AAS 21 (1929), p. 554 print 8 February 1929. The act concerns Brazzaville and Ubanghi Chari. The official indexes give conflicting act dates. The reviewed act date is 1929-02-08, identified at https://www.vatican.va/archive/aas/documents/AAS-21-1929-ocr.pdf printed pp. 553–554; dating clause p. 554.
artifacts.rights_basis: Original historical wording identified in Acta Apostolicae Sedis 21 (1929), pp. 553-554, published by 1930. United States expired-term assessment under 17 U.S.C. 304 and 305; qualifying foreign restoration under 104A(a)(1)(B) receives only the remainder of that term. The preexisting wording remains distinct from modern HTML, creative revision and translations under 103(b). See src/sources/inventories/papal-documents-rights-v1.toml for the primary authorities and jurisdictional limits.
